source.title: Measures of Information Reflect Memorization Patterns
source.authors: Rachit Bansal; Danish Pruthi; Yonatan Belinkov

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied; no garbling or cutoff apparent.
record.tranche_reason: Measures activation entropy and mutual information against memorization and generalization outcomes in several tasks. This tests the informational properties associated with generalization, but not the claim's specified interventions and training conditions.
record.gate_note: The paper studies heuristic and example-level memorization, including shuffled-label settings, and reports validation accuracy alongside activation measures. It does not test whether models that fit arbitrary labels also generalize on natural labels under standard training, nor does it test the listed architecture, optimizer, batch-size, regularization, or width comparisons. OOD context results are reported, but the claim excludes OOD generalization as a separate topic.
record.test_reason: The study tests activation entropy and mutual information as indicators of memorization, rather than any of V1–V8. Section 4 compares natural and shuffled labels, but reports no training accuracy establishing near-perfect random-label fit, so it does not establish V1's coexistence result. Its norm comparisons do not measure V7's magnitude-aware sharpness. The record's tests/T2 classification is therefore incorrect.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors conclude that activation entropy and mutual information distinguish heuristic from example-level memorization and offer a potential model-selection tool. Their findings are comparative: ranking correlations are weaker for some Bias-in-Bios metrics, and values across architectures or capacities may not be directly comparable.
record.recipe_differences: Measures activation information organization in synthetic and natural memorization scenarios; does not reproduce the interventions or comparisons specified in the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary by task, layer, and model family; the authors report that information values across different capacity models may not be directly comparable.

fits_no_version.finding: Increasing induced shortcut correlations lowers validation accuracy and activation entropy while generally increasing neuron-pair mutual information in Colored MNIST and Sentiment Adjectives.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Activation information measures distinguish degrees of heuristic memorization in these controlled settings.

fits_no_version.finding: Increasing training-label shuffling lowers validation accuracy and generally raises entropy and lowers neuron-pair mutual information on MNIST and IMDb. Training accuracy is not reported.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Activation information measures track label-noise conditions, with task- and model-dependent patterns.

fits_no_version.finding: On Bias-in-Bios, mutual information tracks gender extractability; entropy does not consistently distinguish the debiasing conditions. Ranking correlations with fairness gaps are weak, including τ = 0.07 for mutual information versus TPR gap.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Activation information measures have uneven associations with gender encoding and fairness metrics.

fits_no_version.finding: ResNet-18 trained on context-balanced NICO++ reaches 50.08% validation accuracy versus 35.03% with unbalanced contexts, with higher entropy and lower mutual information.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Activation information measures distinguish context-balanced and context-confounded image classifiers.

fits_no_version.finding: Entropy and mutual-information rankings correlate positively with task-specific evaluation rankings, but correlations vary substantially. Norm-based rankings are inconsistent across tasks; magnitude-aware sharpness is not evaluated.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Activation information measures can help rank comparable models in the examined settings, conditional on knowing the relevant memorization type.

record.problems: The findings are comparative and may not be directly comparable across model families, architectures, or capacities. The paper studies small to moderately large networks and says scaling with data and model size needs more research. Several outcomes are described through figures without numerical values in the supplied text; the authors also note wide distributions can make smaller differences difficult to identify.
record.rows_left_out: No rows: the version definitions concern interventions or measurements not tested by this study. Its reported findings concern activation information measures and task-specific validation or OOD outcomes, which do not directly measure any defined version.

untested.parts: Near-perfect random-label training fit alongside above-chance natural-label generalization under the same architecture and recipe; chance-level held-out accuracy with random labels is not explicitly established.
Test error as width increases beyond the width required for zero training error.
Matched convolutional versus fully connected image-classification comparisons and the contribution of local connectivity or initialization.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer generalization under specified tuning regimes.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that recover performance.
Dropout interventions, including dependence on training-set size, dropout strength, augmentation and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness versus training–test gaps, including its ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus random examples and retraining to compare test accuracy.

record.verdict_notes: No extracted rows require correction. Leaving version-linked rows empty is justified. Neither the depth sweep in Appendix C.2 nor the norm comparisons in Appendix D.2 test V2 or V7, respectively.

versions.untested_parts: Does not compare natural-label generalization and random-label fit for the same architectures and recipes.
Does not sweep width across the interpolation threshold or report test error as width increases.
Does not compare convolutional and fully connected networks on the same image task.
Does not compare adaptive optimizers with SGD or test the effects of tuning, weight decay, or optimizer switching.
Does not compare batch sizes or training budgets.
Does not add or remove dropout or weight decay.
Measures entropy and mutual information, but does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness or compare it to norm- and margin-based measures.
Does not remove memorized examples and retrain to measure test accuracy.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
